evals.prompt: Review the shared button change in evals/files/shared-widget-project. The application is runnable, and one continuous recording plus a render report are available under its `evidence/` directory. Inspect the source and every recorded frame without launching another browser; trace every current consumer, state the actual ordered transition, identify which interactive states remain unverified, and distinguish the controlled before variant from historical provenance.
evals.expected_output: The review traces both current consumers, inspects the assembled search and settings pages in the frames that exist, reports the actual ordered transition, preserves the controlled comparison without claiming it is historical provenance, and does not infer consumer or interactive-state coverage from the shared component fixture alone.
assertions: Both SearchPage and SettingsPage are identified as current consumers of the shared button.
The review inspects the assembled consumers and identifies which affected interactive states remain unverified rather than inferring them from Button.js.
The report distinguishes rendered evidence from tests or source inspection.
Any consumer or state not inspected is named as a gap.
The review labels the before capture as a controlled comparison rather than historical provenance.

evals.prompt: Review the modal focus change in evals/files/no-render-project. No browser, rendered page, recording mechanism, or equivalent visual-evidence mechanism is available, but the unit tests pass. Tell me whether the UI change is complete.
evals.expected_output: The review uses the source and tests to identify what they can establish, then hands off the rendered behavior with the missing browser and evidence capability instead of claiming visual completion.
assertions: The response does not claim visual acceptance from passing tests.
The handoff names the missing rendered page or recording capability.
The response preserves the completed source and test evidence.
The response gives a resumable next step for checking the rendered focus behavior.

assertions: The review accepts the project-declared screenshot pair as the evidence form.
The review does not require a GIF when the project declares the equivalent form.
The simulated focus pair is rejected as proof of native focus.
Missing rendered coverage remains a gap rather than a passing visual claim.

evals.prompt: Review the responsive form change in evals/files/responsive-draft-project. The layout switches by replacing the form markup, the input currently holds an in-progress draft, and the project declares no minimum input-size rule. Report the user-visible risks and the smallest source-level corrections to preserve.
evals.expected_output: The review preserves the in-progress draft across the wide/narrow layout change instead of allowing the input remount to discard it. Because the project declares no input-size rule, it keeps the coarse-pointer text input at least 16 CSS pixels so focusing the field does not trigger automatic zoom. It also identifies the rendered states that still need verification.
assertions: The wide/narrow layout change preserves the in-progress draft rather than discarding it with the remounted input.
With no project rule, the coarse-pointer text input remains at least 16 CSS pixels to avoid focus zoom.
The review identifies the affected rendered draft and focused-input states that still need verification.
The review does not treat the source correction as rendered acceptance.

assertions: The review preserves the declared non-scaling stroke behavior and intentional fill geometry.
The review identifies the intentional filled contour and leaves its rendered geometry unproved.
The review checks the target CSS sizes and device-pixel ratios across the shared consumers.
The review treats the missing rendered evidence as a gap.

evals.prompt: Review the spacing and anchored-overlay change in evals/files/spacing-overlay-project. The project supplies its accepted current-build render report and ordered placement timeline under `evidence/`; do not launch another browser, replace its spacing tokens, or substitute another evidence policy. Identify the concrete grouping and overlay failures and report whether the change is complete.
evals.expected_output: The review uses the rendered gap endpoints to distinguish the object and action groups, reports the reversed inter-group and intra-group hierarchy and the heading's separation from its own content, requires outside-click and focusable-Escape dismissal, reports the clipping and missing edge margin, and rejects the repeated flip as an unstable placement that must choose a side that fits.
assertions: Using the rendered gaps and project spacing tokens, the review distinguishes the object and action groups and reports both the inter-group gap smaller than an intra-group gap and the heading separated from its own content.
The review requires outside-click dismissal and Escape while the overlay is focusable, and reports that the fixture has only the outside-click path.
The review finds the overlay clipped at the supported viewport and rejects the missing edge margin and inaccessible action.
The review identifies the flip oscillation and requires flipping only into a side that fits, with no repeated back-and-forth.
